input.brief: Universal DeFi Intelligence: a cross-chain research and swap-quote workspace where execution status is explicit and NEAR ecosystem metrics are source-attributed

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Sentence split by a frame
hero.blueprint: A white or pale ground. One short sentence is broken in two and pushed to the edges: the first half flush to the 32px left margin, the second half flush to the right margin, both on the vertical centre line at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 60px), medium weight. Between them, dead centre on columns 5–8, sits one media frame: 35% of the viewport wide, 16:9, corners 4px, holding a photograph or a working fragment of the product. The frame belongs to a vertical reel: the bottom 60px of the previous frame shows at the top edge of the viewport and the top 60px of the next at the bottom edge, same width, 24px gaps, so the centre column reads as a strip passing through the sentence. The stage is sticky; the reel advances three or four steps while the two halves of the sentence hold their place. Wordmark top-left; three text links and the single action as a small solid button top-right, all at 15px. Bottom-left on columns 1–4: one supporting sentence at 18px, its last line 32px above the bottom edge. The other corners stay empty.
hero.mobile: The halves stack: the first half of the sentence at 9vw flush left under the wordmark, then the frame at full width minus 16px margins and 4:3, then the second half flush right at 9vw. The neighbouring frames show as 28px slivers above and below. The supporting sentence and the action button follow at 16px. The links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: One sentence of four to six words split into two halves of up to about 14 characters each; the frame between them shows what it is about.

photos.title: Sky and space
photos.note: skies, clouds, stars and night skies

photos.alt: Tiny silhouetted figure on a dark ridge under a blue and orange twilight sky
Tiny aeroplane crossing a wide, softly overcast sky
Dark storm clouds hanging over a faint mountain ridge

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One row, three states
sections.blueprint: The product's central row (a task, a transaction, a message, a deploy) is shown three times, one directly beneath the other, in three states: as it arrives, with the pointer on it and its actions revealed, and finished. Each copy is built at true size, 640px wide, with real names, amounts and times, its root marked data-ui; inside it the product's own control borders and radii apply. The copies sit in columns 4–9 with 56px between them and nothing framing them. In columns 1–3, right-aligned and level with each copy, one word at 22px in the soft ink names its state. Columns 10–12 stay empty. The middle copy is live: its checkbox or button works and turns it into the third state. The heading, two to four words at 28–32px, sits on column 4's left edge, 96px above the first copy, with no supporting line.
sections.mobile: Copies stack at full width with 16px margins and stay at true size; a row wider than the screen is cropped at its right end, never shrunk. Each state word sits beneath its copy at 17px in the soft ink, 10px away. 48px separates the three groups. Heading at 26px.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Fixed output, live controls
sections.blueprint: A split the reader operates. Left, columns 1–6: a flat colour field that is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh, edge to edge, holding one thing the product makes (a card, an email, a chart, a rendered page) centred at true size, about 420px wide, root marked data-ui. Right, columns 8–12: a reading column no wider than 44ch, with four or five capability blocks 50vh apart. Each block is a sentence at 28–32px, a paragraph at 17px, and directly beneath it one real control at interface size: a slider, a segmented choice, a toggle, a short text field. Operating a control changes the fixed output on the left at once, and changes persist, so by the last block the reader has configured their own. The section heading, two to four words at 40–44px, opens the right column, 72px from the top.
sections.mobile: The output sits in a sticky field at the top, 42svh tall, cropped to its most telling region, not shrunk. Blocks scroll beneath on the page ground: sentence at 22px, paragraph at 16px, control at full width with 44px targets. The field releases after the last block.

sections.name: Total and its receipt
sections.blueprint: A total at giant size, and beside it the slip that adds up to it. Left, columns 1–6: at the top the heading, two to five words at 40–44px, with a two-line note at 16px; at the bottom-left, anchored to the section's lower edge, the total at clamp(160px, 18vw, 300px) with leading 0.8, and one caption line at 17px under it. The space between heading and total is left empty. Right, columns 8–11: a paper-coloured slip 380–440px wide on the section's contrasting ground, top-aligned with the heading, its bottom edge a zigzag made with clip-path. The slip lists eight to fourteen rows in the text face at 15–16px with tabular numerals, grouped under bold group names; each row has a description on the left, a right-aligned value, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The last row is inverted on a solid ink bar and repeats the total. The slip's values must truly sum to the figure.
sections.mobile: Heading and note come first. The total follows at 40vw, flush left, with its caption. The slip comes last at full width minus 16px margins with its zigzag edge, rows at 15px, and the inverted total row closing it.

sections.name: Question index, one answer
sections.blueprint: Questions on the left, one answer on the right, and the answer changes as the reader moves through the questions. Columns 1–5 list all questions at one size, 18px, with 18px between them; each is preceded by a solid dot 8px across, in the softer ink when idle and in the accent colour when selected. The selected question is in the full ink, the rest in the softer ink. Columns 7–12 hold the answer pane, `position: sticky; top: 120px`: the selected answer at 24–28px in the regular weight, leading 1.3, measure about 30ch, so the answer, not the question, is the large type. Selection follows hover, click and keyboard focus; the pane crossfades in 150ms. The first question is selected on load. A two-word heading in the softer ink is the first line of the list, at the same 18px.
sections.mobile: The list runs full width at 18px. Tapping a question colours its dot and opens its answer directly beneath at 19px, indented to line up with the question text; other answers close. There is no pane and no sticky element.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Uni
references.idea: The product lives in the laptop notch, so the page's navigation is a black notch and the hero is a laptop outline whose notch opens into the app.
references.hero: White page with the hero as a rounded-corner panel inset 24px on all sides, filled with a grainy pastel gradient (pink-peach centre, sky blue down the right edge, orange lower-left). A black pill 300×44px sits top-centre like a laptop notch, holding only the app icon; it is the entire nav. Centred below: a hand-scrawled caps eyebrow, a two-line 48px (3.3vw) headline, two white pill download buttons side by side, one line of tiny grey reassurance. The bottom 40% is a thick black outline of a laptop screen, 960px wide, cropped by the fold, its notch expanded into a dark input bar playing the demo.
references.type: Instrument Sans 500 at 48px with -0.025em tracking for headings; Geist 16px for UI and 12–13px captions. Eyebrows are hand-scrawled marker capitals, irregular and tilted. Only three sizes on the page; the headline is just three times the body.
references.colour: #ffffff #fbdad6 #fce6db #aacbec #f9a070 #000000 — Colour lives only in the hero's grainy pastel gradient; below it the page is white and #fbfbfb with black text. Buttons are near-white pills; the notch is the single black mass.
references.imagery: No photos. A laptop reduced to a thick black rounded outline frames a looping screen recording of the notch UI; eight line icons below. The gradient has visible film grain.
references.layout: Everything on the centre axis. The laptop frame's side strokes continue down the page as hairline rules, so the mockup becomes a 960px content column holding tabs, an icon grid and an FAQ. Three short sections, generous white space, minimal footer.

sections.description: Directly under the device a segmented pill control with three tabs switches the demo. Then a hand-scrawled two-word eyebrow, a centred 32px heading, and a four-by-two grid of thin line icons, each with a two-line 12px centred caption. No cards, borders or backgrounds — just icons on white with about 100px between columns, all inside the hairline-bounded column.

A #fbfbfb band inside the same column. The heading straddles the band's top edge. One rounded, hairline-bordered container holds nine rows separated by hairlines; each row has a 12px medium question at left and a thin plus sign at right. Beneath, a two-line micro footer centred: Roman-numeral year, tiny wordmark, a three-word credit, two legal links.

steal: Shape the navigation like the product's own hardware habitat (here a black notch pill) so the nav itself demonstrates the product.
Extend a device mockup's side strokes down the page as hairline rules so the mockup becomes the content column.
Use a hand-scrawled marker eyebrow above a clean grotesk headline to add one human note to a system-clean page.

references.name: Shelf
references.idea: Saves scattered across a dozen places are funnelled into one searchable shelf, shown literally by tumbling source chips and a panel edge that narrows to a point.
references.hero: An off-white panel sits inside a 12px warm-grey page frame. A compact floating nav about 880px wide: logo left, three links and a lime waitlist button right. Centred stack: a small grey pill badge with a sparkle icon, then a two-line headline in General Sans Semibold at about 5.8vw with tight tracking, one word of which sits on a lime rounded-rectangle highlight; a two-line grey subhead; an email field with its button nested inside one rounded outline, 460px wide. From 75% down, the top of a bordered app window rises, and a larger search bar holding a half-typed query overlaps it with a soft shadow.
references.type: General Sans Semibold for headings (84px hero, 40 to 50px section heads, -0.03em); Switzer for everything else at 14 to 20px, mostly mid-grey. About four sizes. The one flourish is a headline word set on a coloured block.
references.colour: #fbfbf9 #f2f1ed #1b1b19 #9ee86f #e9e9e6 — Warm off-whites and soft charcoal with one lime green: the nav button, the highlighted word, small tags and a full-colour closing block.
references.imagery: Vector mock-ups of the app: a bordered window with sidebar and save cards, an enlarged search field, tiny wireframe thumbnails in step cards. No photography. Angled pill chips with small source icons act as illustration.
references.layout: Centred column inside large rounded off-white panels separated by the grey page frame. Mostly stacked heading-plus-subtext blocks, one left and right split, one narrow accordion column. Panel edges are shaped: one ends in a shallow downward chevron.

sections.description: A centred heading and two-line subtext are partly covered by about nine grey pill chips, each naming a save source with a small icon, rotated at random angles as if dropped. The panel's bottom edge is a shallow V pointing down at centre; from its tip a thin vertical line descends about 80px to a second centred heading, subtext and an empty search field, so the layout itself draws a funnel.

A rounded white panel split in two. Left, from a 10% inset: a small lime tag with icon, a two-line heading at about 50px and two short grey paragraphs, vertically centred. Right, from 53% to 90%: three stacked rounded grey cards about 130px tall, each with a white thumbnail tile at left (a tiny wireframe or the logo) and at right a black numbered dot, a bold one-line title and a line or two of grey text.

A lime rounded block about two-thirds of the width, flanked by narrower lime blocks at left and right separated by 14px gaps, as if cropped from a row. Inside, left-aligned and vertically centred: a 40px heading, two lines of small text and a white email field with the button nested in it. A one-line footer sits on a white strip below.

steal: Shape a section's bottom edge into a chevron and run a hairline from its tip to the next heading, turning 'many into one' into layout.
Overlap an enlarged, half-typed search field onto the product window so the hero shows the key interaction rather than a whole screenshot.
Frame the page as rounded panels inside a slightly darker margin so sections read as stacked sheets.

references.name: Sharplink
references.idea: A crypto treasury presented as precision hardware: chrome machined parts and glass capsules rendered in 3D on deep blue, overlaid with dashed machine-vision tracking boxes.
references.hero: Full-bleed video of exploded brushed-metal components floating on a navy-to-cobalt gradient, covered by a web of thin white dashed lines and small square tracking markers. Logo top-left on a 2% margin; top-right a segmented strip of five dark rectangular tabs in narrow uppercase plus an arrow square. The headline is top-left, two lines at 6.1vw in regular weight with -0.03em tracking, starting 18% down. Under it two stacked rectangular buttons: white with a blue arrow square attached, then a translucent dark one. Bottom row: a stock-exchange badge at left, a three-line lead paragraph at about 1.3vw starting 26% across, and bottom-right a translucent dark news card about 30% wide.
references.type: Archivo regular for headlines (88px in the hero, about 3vw in sections) and 16px body; Archivo Narrow in bold uppercase with wide tracking for nav, buttons and tiny labels. Headlines never go bold: hierarchy comes from size and from fading inactive items to grey.
references.colour: #050c17 #0e3f97 #e6edf7 #a7a8ab #1f6bff #ffffff — One blue family from near-black navy through cobalt to icy white; sections are vertical blue gradients, light or dark. Bright blue appears only as tiny square markers and arrow buttons; chrome grey from the renders.
references.imagery: Chrome and glass 3D objects (exploded device parts, a spike-tipped capsule holding icons) lit coolly, often with dashed annotation lines or shown as dotted wireframes; full-bleed in the hero, floating free at the right in later sections.
references.layout: 2% margins and square corners everywhere. Sections are full-viewport gradient fields with a headline at left and a 3D object or data card at right; lists run as label, title and paragraph in two columns. Tiny blue square bullets mark section starts.

sections.description: Light icy-gradient section. A two-line headline in grey-blue at about 3vw at the left, with a small paragraph far below it at bottom-left. Centre: a tall 3:4 card with a navy-to-cobalt vertical gradient, a tiny uppercase label, a rising line chart over a faint dotted grid, and a full-width dark button at its base. Right third: three faint, nearly transparent rows, each with a small numbered tag, one line of text and a ghosted line drawing.

Pinned list beside a 3D object. Left 60%: stacked rows, each with a tiny uppercase label, a two-line title at about 1.3vw in a first column and a short paragraph in a second column starting 26% across. Only the active row is at full contrast; the rest are dimmed to roughly 40%. Right 40%: a chrome-and-glass capsule about 80% of the viewport tall whose interior icon changes per row. The ground shifts from icy white to deep cobalt partway through.

A black panel inset by 2% on a navy ground with small blue square markers at its corners. Logo mark top-left; a two-line statement at about 2vw at the left, first line white and second line grey; two rectangular buttons below. A dotted wireframe version of the capsule fills the right half. Under the panel, a tiny uppercase label at left and a small button at right.

Cobalt gradient footer: a newsletter line with an underlined email field at left, three small link columns across the middle and right, exchange badge and legal microtext below. The wordmark closes the page in letters spanning the full width, cropped by the bottom edge and fading from white at the top to transparent.

steal: Overlay a 3D render with thin dashed lines and tiny square markers linking its parts, as if a vision system were tracking the object.
Build buttons as square-cornered rectangles with a separate coloured arrow square attached to the right edge.
In a pinned list beside a 3D object, dim every row except the active one and change what sits inside the object for each row.
references.media: A full-bleed 12s loop of 3D chrome and glass objects covers the whole fold, with text docked in the four corners straight on it. Below: a 3D capsule pinned in the right third while a list of claims scrolls on the left, its inner emblem swapping per row, a dark card sliding over it that turns the covered part into a dashed wireframe, a sticky portrait video of chrome pipes at the right edge, and a full-width wordmark canvas cropped by the bottom of the viewport; square corners throughout.
references.motion: The hero is composed at 400ms with the video playing and no preloader (load 21.3s), and Lenis runs four pins over fixed layers: one fixed gradient layer behind everything crossfades the grounds, the capsule stays pinned across three sections as each claim brightens from about 40% to full, and the manifesto fills character by character (423 split characters). The workhorse ease is cubic-bezier(.455,.03,.515,.955), on 57 observed opacity, background and colour transitions at .25-.3s.
